uiLanguage.name: Module language
uiLanguage.hint: Language of Update Guard on this device. "Like Foundry" follows Foundry's language.

theme.name: Look
theme.hint: Signature shows the windows on warm paper, Foundry keeps them dark like the rest of Foundry.

windowMode.name: After an update
windowMode.hint: What happens at the start of the world when something changed since the last start. Only the active GM sees it.

goodAfter.name: Minutes without a module error
goodAfter.hint: A start counts as one that ran well when the world stayed open this long without an error from a module. That state is the one the way back leads to.

guard.name: Update Guard
guard.label: Open Update Guard
guard.hint: What changed since the last start, the check before an update and the way back.

SUG.gmOnly: Update Guard is for the GM.
SUG.Honest: Update Guard runs only in a started world and installs nothing itself. If the world does not start after an update, the export helps. All compatibility data comes from the authors of the packages.

Changes.title: What changed
Changes.noHistory: No state is recorded yet. The state of every start is recorded by the active GM.
Changes.firstStart: This is the first recorded start. Changes show from the next start on.
Changes.none: Nothing changed since the last state.
Changes.removedIncompatible: {title} {version} is gone. Its manifest declared {compat}, which does not fit Foundry {core}, so Foundry may have dropped it.
Changes.notice: Update Guard: {count} changes since the last start. Open it from the settings tab of the sidebar.

Problem.minimum: needs Foundry {minimum} or newer, this is {core}.
Problem.maximum: is declared up to Foundry {maximum}, this is {core}.
Problem.missingDependency: needs the module {id}, which is not installed.
Problem.dependencyVersion: needs {id} in the range {minimum} to {maximum}, installed is {version}.
Problem.missingSystem: needs the game system {id}, this world runs {system}.
Problem.otherSystem: is made for the systems {systems}, this world runs {system}.
Problem.systemRange: is made for {system} from {minimum} to {maximum}, installed is {version}.

AVAIL.UNVERIFIED_BUILD: not verified for this Foundry build
AVAIL.UNVERIFIED_GENERATION: not verified for this Foundry generation
AVAIL.UNVERIFIED_SYSTEM: not verified for the installed game system
AVAIL.REQUIRES_CORE_UPGRADE_UNSTABLE: needs a newer Foundry that is not stable yet

Errors.title: Errors since the start
Errors.since: Counted since this page was loaded on
Errors.other: Errors from Foundry or code that cannot be assigned

Check.invalidTarget: That is not a version. Use 15 or 14.371.
Check.blockedOffline: Look for newer versions shows whether one exists.
Check.deprecatedBreaks: Calls Foundry functions that are removed in {until} ({count} calls). The target is {target}.
Check.deprecatedCalls: Calls deprecated Foundry functions ({count} calls, removal in {until}).
Check.compatSilent: Foundry's compatibility mode is set to silent, so deprecated calls are not reported and not counted.
Check.noProbe: The deprecation counter is not installed, deprecated calls are not counted.
Check.compatFilter: Foundry's compatibility patterns filter some messages, so some deprecated calls may not be counted.

REASON.maximumLow: Declared only up to a Foundry older than {target}, and no newer version is known.
REASON.minimumFits: The minimum version fits {target}, but {target} is not verified.
REASON.maximumFits: The maximum fits {target}, but there is no minimum or verified version.
REASON.noData: The manifest has no compatibility data.
REASON.latestVerified: The newer version {version} is verified for {target}, the installed one is not.
REASON.latestNotBlocked: The newer version {version} is not blocked for {target}, but not verified either.

EVIDENCE.noNewer: {source}: no version newer than the installed one

ERR.blocked: the browser could not reach it, because of missing CORS permission, no network or a blocked connection
ERR.invalid: the answer was not what was expected
ERR.otherPackage: the manifest belongs to another package
ERR.rateLimit: the limit of requests is used up for now

Online.sends: Check online sends the IDs of the game system and the active modules ({count} IDs), one request each, to forge-vtt.com, the public package list of The Forge.
Online.sendsMore: For a package that list does not know, its manifest address is requested from the host named there. Nothing else leaves your browser: no world data, no names, no settings. Like every request from a web page, it carries the address of this Foundry server. Answers stay in memory for one hour and requests are spaced out. Nothing is sent before you click.
Online.stale: The target changed since this check. The ratings use the answers, the answers stay the same.
Online.forge: Package list of The Forge: {ok} answered, {notListed} not listed, {failed} failed.
Online.failed: The online check stopped with an error, see the console.
Online.hint: Asks the public package list of The Forge for newer versions. Nothing leaves your browser before that.

Deprecated.title: Deprecated calls
Deprecated.hint: Modules that called Foundry functions marked as deprecated since this page was loaded. Foundry removes them in a later version, which makes this the clearest sign for the next update.
Deprecated.other: Deprecated calls from Foundry itself or code that cannot be assigned

Export.hint: One file with every version, the rating for the target, what does not fit, errors and deprecated calls.
Export.title: Update Guard export
Export.sources: Package list of The Forge: {forgeOk} answered, {forgeNone} not listed, {forgeFailed} failed. Manifests: {manifestOk} read, {manifestFailed} failed.

Checklist.title: Checklist before the update
Checklist.export: Save the export below as text or JSON. If the world does not start after the update, it is the record of what was installed.
Checklist.snapshot: In Foundry's setup, back up everything with "{snapshot}" before you update.
Checklist.copy: Copy the world folder, or try the update on a copy of the world first.
Checklist.order: Update in this order: Foundry, then the game system, then the modules marked update needed.
Checklist.test: Start the world as GM and let Update Guard do a test run.

Back.core: Foundry ran {good} then, now it is {current}.
Back.coreNote: Foundry itself cannot be changed from inside a world. A Foundry build comes from your licenses page on foundryvtt.com or from an installer you kept. A world that a newer Foundry has migrated does not open in an older one without a backup made before.
Back.verifyHint: Asks api.github.com whether the release of that version exists and has the manifest file.
Back.guess: The address is derived from the installed manifest address. It is a guess until you check it.
Back.noDerive: No older manifest address can be derived from the installed one.
Back.nothingToDo: Every module has the version of the last good state.
Back.copyFailed: The address could not be copied.
Back.verifyFound: The release {tag} exists and has the manifest file.
Back.verifyNoFile: The release {tag} exists but has no manifest file with that name.
Back.verifyNotFound: No release for that version was found under the usual tag names.

step.setup: Leave the world with "{setup}". Foundry installs and restores packages only on the setup screen.
step.snapshot: If you made a snapshot or backup before the update, restore it there. "{snapshot}" is the button that makes one.
step.install: Otherwise open {modules}, then {install}, paste the {manifest} of the older version and install it. Check the version in the module list afterwards.
step.world: Start the world and let Update Guard do a test run.

Back.olderSame: Foundry {core}, {system}. All modules still have the same version.
Back.current: The current state is your good state.
Back.currentSub: If an update breaks something, this is where you see how to get back.
Back.none: There is no good state yet.
Back.noneSub: A test run without errors creates one.

History.title: Recorded states
History.hint: The last 12 different states. A state is saved only when something changed, otherwise only its date is updated.

SELFTEST.Title: Self test
SELFTEST.Hint: Checks after an update that everything the module relies on is there.
SELFTEST.NewVersions: Foundry is newer than the verified version ({versions}). Run the self test if something looks wrong.
SELFTEST.VersionRules: The module's version comparison differs from Foundry's.
SELFTEST.Availability: Foundry's package availability codes are missing or have other names.
SELFTEST.Packages: The installed packages could not be read as expected.
SELFTEST.ActiveGM: Foundry does not tell who the active GM is.
SELFTEST.History: The stored history could not be read.
SELFTEST.Watch: The early watch for errors is not running.
SELFTEST.Probe: The counter for deprecated calls is not in Foundry's compatibility patterns.
SELFTEST.Save: Foundry cannot save a file from here.
SELFTEST.CoreTexts: Foundry texts used in the steps are missing: {keys}

DEBUG.Title: Debug file
DEBUG.Hint: One file about all of Sephral's modules in this world, for bug reports. It contains chat text and whispers.
DEBUG.Saved: Debug file saved: {file}. It contains chat text and whispers, check it before you share it.

Run.troubleSub: Below you see which ones and where. Switch them off one by one or let the search find the culprit.
Run.troubleOneSub: Below you see which one and where. Switch it off or let the search find the culprit.
Run.testedSub: Test run of {at}: {checks} checks without errors.
Run.ranSub: This state has been running without errors since {at}.
Run.changedSub: A test run shows in half a minute whether everything still works.
Run.firstSub: Today's state is recorded. After the next update you see here what is different.
Run.untestedSub: A test run shows in half a minute whether everything works.

Update.blocked: {count} modules do not run on Foundry {target} yet.
Update.blockedSub: {names}. The authors of the other {open} have not confirmed it yet.
Update.blockedOne: One module does not run on Foundry {target} yet.
Update.blockedOneSub: {names}. The authors of the other {open} have not confirmed it yet.
Update.blockedOneTab: Not yet: one module blocks it
Update.breaksSub: They call functions that are removed there.
Update.breaksOne: One module could break in Foundry {target}.
Update.breaksOneSub: It calls functions that are removed there.
Update.update: {count} modules need an update before Foundry {target}.
Update.updateOne: One module needs an update before Foundry {target}.
Update.openSub: The authors just have not confirmed it yet ({open}). That is normal for a new version.

Group.blockedHint: The authors name a maximum below {target}.
Group.breaksHint: Calls functions that are removed in {target}.
Group.waitingHint: Normal for a new version, the authors catch up.

Trial.title: Test run
Trial.hint: Opens sheets and windows for a moment and closes them again. Your world is not changed.
Trial.summaryGood: {checks} checks, no module threw an error.
Trial.deprecated: {count} outdated calls came up on the way. They are listed under Can I update?
Trial.failed: The test run stopped, the console has the details.

Search.hint: Finds the module behind a problem: switch off, look, narrow it down. In the end everything is as it was.
Search.title: Find the module
Search.intro: Update Guard switches modules off and reloads the world. Each time you look whether the problem is still there. After a few rounds the module is known and everything is as it was.
Search.introChanged: First under suspicion is what changed since {since}. That is {count}.
Search.introAll: No module changed since the last good state, so all {count} active modules are under suspicion.
Search.others: Others are logged in as well ({count}). They notice nothing until they reload.
Search.nothing: There are no modules to search.
Search.testing: {off} of {total} suspects are off right now. Try what did not work. Is the problem still there?
Search.foundText: With this module the problem was there, without it the problem was gone. All modules are back on until you decide.
Search.noneChangedTitle: It is not one of the changed modules.
Search.noneChangedText: The problem stayed although all of them were off. All modules are back on.
Search.noneAllText: The problem stayed although the modules were off. So it is in Foundry, the game system or the world itself.

Off.title: Switch off a module
Off.text: {name} is switched off in this world and the world reloads. You can switch it on again in Foundry's module manager at any time.
Off.also: These need it and go off with it: {names}.
